items.title: Το σύζευγμα αντισώματος-φαρμάκου δείχνει υποσχόμενα πρώιμα αποτελέσματα στη δοκιμή Φάσης Ι σε ασθενείς με σάρκωμα
items.titleOriginal: Antibody-drug conjugate shows promising early results in Phase I trial in sarcoma patients
items.description: Ένα συζυγές αντισώματος-φαρμάκου, ένας τύπος φαρμάκου που στοχεύει και εισέρχεται στα καρκινικά κύτταρα όπως ο Δούρειος Ίππος, έχει δείξει πολλά υποσχόμενα πρώιμα αποτελέσματα σε διάφορους τύπους σαρκώματος μαλακών μορίων σε μια δοκιμή Φάσης Ι. Τα ευρήματα παρουσιάστηκαν στο 38ο Συμπόσιο EORTC-NCI-AACR για τους Μοριακούς Στόχους και τη Θεραπευτική Καρκίνου στη Βαρκελώνη της Ισπανίας.
items.descriptionOriginal: An antibody-drug conjugate, a type of drug that targets and enters cancer cells like a Trojan Horse, has shown promising early results across diverse types of soft tissue sarcoma in a Phase I trial. The findings were presented at the 38th EORTC-NCI-AACR Symposium on Molecular Targets and Cancer Therapeutics in Barcelona, Spain.

items.title: Οι ΗΠΑ αναπτύσσουν υπερυπολογιστή με 2.688 τσιπ NVIDIA για να επιταχύνουν την επιστημονική ανακάλυψη
items.titleOriginal: US deploys supercomputer with 2,688 NVIDIA chips to accelerate scientific discovery
items.description: Το Argonne Leadership Computing Facility (ALCF) του Εθνικού Εργαστηρίου Argonne επεκτείνει την υπηρεσία συμπερασμάτων του, με επικεφαλής την ανάπτυξη ενός νέου συστήματος μεγάλης κλίμακας που ονομάζεται Tara, που βασίζεται στην αρχιτεκτονική υπερυπολογιστών. Η επέκταση φέρνει ένα ευρύτερο φάσμα μοντέλων AI/super Intelligence (SI) και ροές εργασιών πρακτόρων απευθείας στην επιστημονική έρευνα. Το upgra…
items.descriptionOriginal: Argonne National Laboratory’s Argonne Leadership Computing Facility (ALCF) is expanding its inference service, led by the deployment of a new large-scale system called Tara, built on supercomputing architecture. The expansion brings a wider array of AI/super intelligence (SI) models and agentic workflows directly into scientific research. The upgrade arrives at a pivotal moment for American science. Going beyond simple prompts, researchers can now use autonomous AI agents to plan experiments, write code, and run lab instruments at scale. “The ALCF has long provided the computing resources researchers need to pursue science at scale,” said Venkat Vishwanath, SI team lead at the ALCF. ​“As inference and agentic workflows take on a growing role in science, we are evolving to provide new services and tools that complement our computing systems and help scientists be more productive in their research.” Advancement in memory and speed Tara is a powerhouse built alongside Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) on its exascale-class HPE Cray Supercomputing EX4000 architecture. The supercomputer packs 672 computing nodes and 2,688 NVIDIA GH200 Grace Hopper Superchips. Tara delivers roughly 100 times the GPU memory previously available on the platform. Tara does not stand alone. Argonne also unveiled Minerva, an eight-node system built with World Wide Technology and powered by 64 NVIDIA B200 GPUs. At the same time, the lab tripled its Metis platform to six SambaRacks equipped with 96 SambaNova SN40L chips. Paired with the existing Sophia platform, this hardware expansion supports more than 50 advanced models, including open-weight large language models, scientific foundation models, and computer vision tools. All of these capabilities operate inside a secure, on-premises environment built to safeguard sensitive research data. Real-world science in motion Offering inference as a shared national resource gives individual research teams affordable access to massive AI models via APIs or a chat-like interface. These scientific agents connect directly to supercomputing power and specialized tools to prepare simulations, optimize code, and analyze experimental data in real time. “We’re moving to a point where agentic workflows are playing a much bigger role in the scientific process,” said ALCF Director of Science Katherine Riley. ​“We’re seeing researchers put agents to work to connect scientific tools, automate multistep calculations and data analysis, and use experimental results to help determine what to investigate next.” Early applications already show how this infrastructure accelerates the Department of Energy’s (DOE’s) Genesis Mission for discovery science, national security, and energy innovation. Argonne’s ChemGraph framework turns plain descriptions of chemistry and materials problems into automated simulations and analyses. Meanwhile, the SYNAPS-I project demonstrated autonomous experiments at a DOE light source, where an AI agent scanned a microelectronics sample, analyzed the visuals with computer vision models, and steered the instrument directly to a target boundary. For scientists across the ALCF user community and DOE national laboratories, the limiting factor is shifting from access to raw computing power to imagination. Vishwanath highlighted the payoff of embedding inference directly into simulations and experiments. Researchers can now tackle far larger problems and move from an initial spark of an idea to a breakthrough faster than ever before.

items.title: Αποκλειστικό: Από την εγκατάλειψη της Μηχανικής για τη μουσική έως την απόκτηση ενός Grammy, το «Varuvaaiy» του Devan Ekambaram γράφει ιστορία για τα Ταμίλ
items.titleOriginal: Exclusive: From Leaving Engineering for Music to Earning a Grammy Nod, Devan Ekambaram’s ‘Varuvaaiy’ Makes History For Tamil
items.description: "Uruvaai arivil olirvaai Kanna! Είμαι τόσο χαρούμενος που είμαι εδώ!" Λάμψε μέσα στη συνείδησή μου, Μπορείς. ξεχύσω σαν το νέκταρ της ζωής μου. Στην ποίηση του Σουμπραμάνια Μπχαράτι, η εικόνα της αφοσίωσης και της αγάπης συχνά φτάνει πέρα ​​από την άμεση στιγμή. Πάνω από έναν αιώνα αφότου γράφτηκαν τα λόγια του, μια από τις συνθέσεις του βρήκε ένα νέο μουσικό l…
items.descriptionOriginal: "Uruvaai arivil olirvaai Kanna! Uyirin amudhaai pozhivaai Kanna!" Shine within my consciousness, O Kanna; pour forth as the nectar of my life. In Subramania Bharati's poetry, the imagery of devotion and love often reaches beyond the immediate moment. More than a century after his words were written, one of his compositions has found a new musical life — this time, on a global stage. But when the Grammy nominations were being announced on 16 November, the man behind that contemporary interpretation was nowhere near a television screen. Back from a project in Sri Lanka, Devan Ekambaram could not bring himself to watch the nominations unfold. He went instead to a temple. "I was too nervous to watch," he recalls. At 6.47 pm IST, his phone lit up. A friend in Los Angeles sent him a message: "Congratulations!" His phone soon filled with 80 or 90 similar messages. "I realised what had happened and immediately broke down crying," he says. Released independently in August 2026, Varuvaaiy became the first Tamil song nominated for a Grammy. The song that had brought him to this moment was Varuvaaiy , an independent Tamil recording he composed and produced with vocalist Subhiksha Rangarajan, known as Susha. It had been nominated for Best Global Music Performance at the 69th Grammy Awards, becoming the first Tamil song to receive a Grammy nomination. For Ekambaram, the moment carried a childhood dream: watching Michael Jackson win a Grammy for Thriller and hearing presenter Whoopi Goldberg urge young viewers to hold on to their dreams. It was also a milestone reached without a family music legacy. "I come from a family of doctors and engineers. Nobody is in the art field, and I had to embark on this journey all alone," he says. A childhood tuned to music Growing up in New Jersey, often one of the few Indian children in his neighbourhood, Ekambaram found it difficult to fit in. Music became a source of confidence . His mother introduced him to different genres, while programmes such as American Bandstand and Solid Gold showed him performers building careers around music. He began playing guitar between the seventh and tenth grades, then joined the school choir and marching band. He learnt to listen for harmonies and how musical parts fitted together, and began recording at home. "I knew my weakness, but I found my strength," he says. He developed his musical identity through choir, harmony and arranging. Growing up in New Jersey, Devan Ekambaram found his first musical inspiration through school choirs, guitars and American television. The Grammys entered his imagination around this time. "I remember watching Michael Jackson win for Thriller , and hearing presenter Whoopi Goldberg urge young viewers to hold on to their dreams, come what may. And that became my dream," he says. At 19 or 20, while studying electrical engineering at the University of Illinois, he explored music opportunities during a college break in India. He eventually left engineering and moved to Chennai at 21. "I just quit my engineering degree in the US and came here with no support and no direction. It was the scariest thing because I never saw anyone do this growing up," he says. Building a life in music — and finding the right voice Ekambaram's move to Chennai gradually opened doors. His 1998 album Kamban Oru Kannile , made with S P Charan, caught A R Rahman's attention and led to work on Kadhalar Dhinam . He made his playback debut with "Oh Maria" in 1999 and went on to sing on more than 500 film soundtracks, while also working as a composer, voice artist, and vocal arranger. He had contributed to Grammy-winning projects such as Winds of Samsara (2015) and Divine Tides (2022). But this time, he wanted to create something that was unmistakably his own: an independent album reimagining the poetry of Subramania Bharati through contemporary arrangements. For the first single, he had a particular voice in mind. Ekambaram had met Subhiksha Rangarajan, known as Susha, back in 2007, when they appeared on the television programme Coffee with Anu . He had wanted to collaborate with her ever since, but the opportunity never quite came together. When he began working on the Bharati project, he reached out to her again. Years after meeting vocalist Susha in 2007, Ekambaram brought her into his independent project celebrating Subramania Bharati's poetry. Photograph: ( Instagram/@sushasings ) In June 2026, Susha arrived at his home studio with her mother, Lakshmi Rangarajan. The composition they were about to record was one Lakshmi had taught her, set to a tune by L Krishnan that was already around 40 to 50 years old. What followed was an unusually quick coming together of ideas . Ekambaram asked Susha to sing, and the recording took shape over the next two to three hours. For him, her voice brought together the musical sensibilities the song needed. Trained in Carnatic music and having studied jazz at the University of Toronto, Susha could move between the classical foundation of the composition and the contemporary sound he wanted to create. She had also been building her own independent music career, including through NEXA Music, an initiative by A R Rahman and Clinton Cerejo that selected her among 24 artistes in 2019. "Without her singing, nobody would have listened to the song," Ekambaram says. Giving an old poem a new sound He wanted to rebuild the traditional arrangement while retaining the melody's character. "I just gave it a makeover," he says. "I looked at it thinking, how I would want to hear this?" He wanted to make the form inviting to a new generation of listeners unfamiliar with Carnatic music without flattening its identity. Set in raga Desh, the arrangement brings Carnatic phrasing together with piano, slide guitar, acoustic guitar, bass and tabla. Ekambaram played keyboards and produced the track. It features pianist Anil Srinivasan, slide guitarist Prakash Sontakke, guitarist Naveen Samson, bassist Joseph John and tabla player Sarvajit Krishna Mohan. Roshan Sebastian mixed and mastered it. The collaboration was largely remote: Susha recorded at Ekambaram's home studio, while the instrumentalists sent their parts from elsewhere. "I coordinated the musicians and worked with Sebastian on the final mix. The result was a three-minute-and-26-second recording released independently on 12 August 2026," he says. Susha's Carnatic training and jazz influences shaped Varuvaaiy, a contemporary interpretation of a century-old Tamil composition. Susha's contribution was central to the sound he had imagined. "Without her singing, nobody would have listened to the song," Ekambaram says. Her Carnatic training, jazz studies at the University of Toronto and contemporary sensibility shaped the recording. In 2019, she was among 24 artistes selected for NEXA Music, an initiative by A R Rahman and Clinton Cerejo. Her debut album, Love Language , arrived in August 2026. Written more than a century ago, the poem's exact date is unknown, though it is believed to date from Bharati's years in Pondicherry. Its imagery calls for a force to enter human thought and dispel darkness, and has been read as a metaphor for resisting oppression and colonial rule. That purpose appealed to Ekambaram. Rather than create a new song with contemporary lyrics, he wanted to bring a poet whose words shaped Tamil public life to younger listeners. "I thought this had a purpose," he says. He hoped a fresh musical arrangement would allow his children's generation to encounter Bharati's language without feeling distanced by it. A release against the clock Getting the single out in time required a difficult decision. Ekambaram says labels he approached were hesitant because the underlying work was in the public domain, and the permissions process threatened to delay the release. "With the Grammy submission deadline approaching, I chose to release the track independently and complete the distribution myself. But I never imagined how well it would work," he recalls. Rooted in raga Desh, the recording blends Carnatic nuances with jazz influences, guitars, piano and tabla. He had submitted work before and contributed to Grammy-winning projects, but this time concentrated on Varuvaaiy , preparing its streaming links for the Best Global Music Performance category. The category had 526 submissions, he says, and seeing the names on the ballot made a nomination feel far from certain. On nomination morning, the song had around 300 YouTube views, according to Ekambaram. As the news spread, the count rose to about 35,000. Messages of appreciation came from musicians including Scott Hoying of Pentatonix and Chandrika Tandon. What comes after the nomination The recognition arrived as Ekambaram questioned what came next. He had considered continuing in Chennai or returning to the United States if work did not move forward. He wanted to build a body of work listeners could associate with him, not a film or star. He worried that short-lived online trends left less room for songs that stay with people. The February 2027 Grammy ceremony will see Varuvaaiy compete alongside recordings by internationally acclaimed musicians. "The nomination has renewed my resolve to make independent music, compose and experiment rather than rely only on past successes. To think that I almost gave up and left for L. A., but we never know when opportunities will come. Today, I'm glad I continued on the path," he says. Ekambaram credits mentors including Madhav Das at Magnus Sound, choir director Ruth Lane McIntyre and the high-school teacher who encouraged him to sing. He wishes they could have witnessed the announcement. The larger Bharati album is now the next step. Ekambaram says it will contain 10 to 12 contemporary interpretations, with the tracks already taking shape and around two months of work remaining at the time of the interview. He is also waiting for a bilingual Tamil-Telugu film for which he composed the music to reach audiences. The ceremony is scheduled for February 2027 in Los Angeles, where Varuvaaiy will compete alongside recordings by Ang lique Kidjo, Rosal a, Shakira and Burna Boy. Winning would be wonderful, he says, but the nomination has already given him something deeply valuable. For Ekambaram, the nomination is already a milestone: bringing Tamil poetry and music to a global audience. "I don't care whether I win the category or not," he says. "I've been a catalyst in placing Tamil music on the global map. That is my win." More than a century after Bharati wrote the poem, its words have travelled into a new musical language: first through a melody passed down across generations, then through a contemporary arrangement shaped by musicians working across genres and distances. Now, listeners far beyond Tamil-speaking communities are being invited to hear it, too, today. That, perhaps, is the lasting possibility of Varuvaaiy . A poem written in another time has not been left behind in it. It has been given another voice, another audience and another chance to be understood. And somewhere, a listener encountering Bharati for the first time may follow the song back to the words that began it all.

items.title: Ο αμερικανικός στρατός πιστοποιεί την πρώτη μπαταρία Patriot στο IBCS στη Νότια Κορέα, απελευθερώνοντας τα ραντάρ του
items.titleOriginal: US Army certifies first Patriot battery on IBCS in South Korea, freeing its radars
items.description: Η Delta Battery, 6ο Τάγμα, 52ο Σύνταγμα Πυροβολικού Αεράμυνας, έγινε η πρώτη επιχειρησιακή μπαταρία Patriot του Στρατού των ΗΠΑ που πιστοποιήθηκε στο Integrated Battle Command System (IBCS). Η Όγδοη Στρατιά ανακοίνωσε το ορόσημο στις 18 Νοεμβρίου για τη μονάδα, μέρος της 35ης Ταξιαρχίας Πυροβολικού Αεράμυνας στη Δημοκρατία της Κορέας. Ξέσπασε από μονάδες Silos Patriot…
items.descriptionOriginal: Delta Battery, 6th Battalion, 52nd Air Defense Artillery Regiment, became the first operational U.S. Army Patriot battery certified on the Integrated Battle Command System (IBCS). Eighth Army announced the milestone on Nov. 18 for the unit, part of the 35th Air Defense Artillery Brigade in the Republic of Korea. Breaking out of Silos Patriot units have traditionally relied on legacy, siloed weapon networks. With IBCS, Delta Battery’s Soldiers moved onto the system’s Integrated Fire Control Network and proved they could separate sensors and launchers from the battery’s fire control unit. That separation lets the battery spread out its equipment instead of keeping it clustered in one spot. The Army describes the goal as “best sensor, best shooter,” pairing whichever connected radar has the best track with the launcher best placed to engage. A Patriot battery pairs a radar, a fire control unit and launchers that fire interceptors such as the PAC-2 GEM-T and PAC-3 MSE. A connected radar can supply tracking data, and fire control personnel can use it to assign an engagement to a suitable launcher elsewhere on the network. Crews gain flexibility in where they place equipment while still operating as a formation. Dispersal reduces how much equipment sits in any one location, though coordination still depends on connectivity among sensors, launchers and command elements. Readiness on Peninsula The Army said the forward-deployed certification enhances the 35th Brigade’s “Fight Tonight” readiness. It proves the unit can integrate modern air defense technology and defend critical assets against complex regional missile threats. More Patriot units in the battalion are expected to certify on IBCS in the coming weeks. That would prepare the battalion for follow-on distributed command and control operations, in which crews coordinate engagements across a shared network. The release gave no date for those certifications beyond the coming weeks. What remains unproven The announcement covers a unit certification, not a combat test. The release offers no survivability data for a dispersed battery, and any gain depends on sensor coverage, track quality and network availability. Eighth Army also did not say that THAAD , Aegis or F-35 sensors in Korea were linked through IBCS during the certification. The milestone applies to Delta Battery alone for now. A wider Army push IBCS is a Northrop Grumman system meant to connect sensors and weapons across the Army’s air and missile defense force. Earlier tests tied it to the new Lower Tier Air and Missile Defense Sensor radar and to the Navy’s SM-6 missile, according to earlier reporting. Lockheed Martin’s battle management prototype for Guam also draws on IBCS data, according to earlier reporting. Northrop Grumman has said IBCS fuses data from multiple sensors so commanders can pick the best shooter against incoming threats, according to earlier reporting. Newer interceptors are being designed around it too. Lockheed Martin’s PAC-3 Edge and PAC-3 ACE are designed to work with IBCS, and the Army has sought cheaper interceptors that must integrate with it. For forces in Korea, the certification puts that connected approach in the hands of a forward-deployed Patriot crew. The next test is whether other batteries can share tracks and coordinate engagements across the battalion.

items.title: Γιατί τα φάρμακα δεν δρουν το ίδιο σε όλους – Ο ρόλος των γονιδίων στις παρενέργειες
items.titleOriginal: Γιατί τα φάρμακα δεν δρουν το ίδιο σε όλους – Ο ρόλος των γονιδίων στις παρενέργειες
items.description: Έχετε αναρωτηθεί ποτέ γιατί ένα φάρμακο που βοηθά κάποιον άλλον μπορεί να μην έχει την ίδια αποτελεσματικότητα σε εσάς ; Ή γιατί ορισμένοι ασθενείς εμφανίζουν έντονες παρενέργειες από μια θεραπεία που άλλοι ανέχονται χωρίς ιδιαίτερα προβλήματα; Η ηλικία , η κατάσταση της υγείας , οι συνυπάρχουσες παθήσεις και η ταυτόχρονη λήψη άλλων φαρμάκων μπορούν να επηρεάσουν την ανταπόκριση στη θεραπεία.…
items.descriptionOriginal: Έχετε αναρωτηθεί ποτέ γιατί ένα φάρμακο που βοηθά κάποιον άλλον μπορεί να μην έχει την ίδια αποτελεσματικότητα σε εσάς ; Ή γιατί ορισμένοι ασθενείς εμφανίζουν έντονες παρενέργειες από μια θεραπεία που άλλοι ανέχονται χωρίς ιδιαίτερα προβλήματα; Η ηλικία , η κατάσταση της υγείας , οι συνυπάρχουσες παθήσεις και η ταυτόχρονη λήψη άλλων φαρμάκων μπορούν να επηρεάσουν την ανταπόκριση στη θεραπεία. Ωστόσο, ένας ακόμη παράγοντας φαίνεται ότι παίζει σημαντικό ρόλο: Το γενετικό μας προφίλ. Νέα μελέτη, με επικεφαλής ερευνητές του Πανεπιστημίου του Πίτσμπουργκ, που δημοσιεύθηκε στο Science Translational Medicine , διαπίστωσε ότι όλοι οι συμμετέχοντες ενός μεγάλου και πληθυσμιακά ποικιλόμορφου δείγματος σχεδόν 100.000 ανθρώπων έφεραν τουλάχιστον μία γενετική παραλλαγή που μπορεί να επηρεάσει την αποτελεσματικότητα ή την τοξικότητα ορισμένων φαρμάκων. Ακόμη πιο ενδιαφέρον είναι ότι σχεδόν 1 στους 4 συμμετέχοντες είχε λάβει συνταγή για τουλάχιστον ένα φάρμακο που επηρεάζεται από γενετική παραλλαγή την οποία έφερε. Τα ευρήματα υποστηρίζουν την υιοθέτηση μιας πιο εξατομικευμένης προσέγγισης στη συνταγογράφηση, που θα λαμβάνει υπόψη και τις γενετικές ιδιαιτερότητες κάθε ασθενούς. Τι έδειξε η μελέτη σε σχεδόν 100.000 ανθρώπους Οι ερευνητές αξιοποίησαν δεδομένα από το ερευνητικό πρόγραμμα All of Us των Εθνικών Ινστιτούτων Υγείας των ΗΠΑ (NIH), εξετάζοντας τη συχνότητα εμφάνισης 16 γνωστών γενετικών παραλλαγών που σχετίζονται με την αποτελεσματικότητα ή την τοξικότητα διαφορετικών φαρμάκων . Το αποτέλεσμα ήταν εντυπωσιακό: Το 100% των συμμετεχόντων έφερε τουλάχιστον 1 από τις παραλλαγές που εξετάστηκαν – κατά μέσο όρο, μάλιστα, οι συμμετέχοντες έφεραν 9 μεταλλάξεις. Στη συνέχεια, οι επιστήμονες συνέκριναν τα γενετικά δεδομένα με τους ιατρικούς φακέλους των συμμετεχόντων, αναζητώντας περιπτώσεις στις οποίες είχε συνταγογραφηθεί φάρμακο με γνωστή αλληλεπίδραση με κάποια από τις παραλλαγές αυτές. Διαπίστωσαν ότι το 24,4% είχε λάβει συνταγή για τουλάχιστον 1 τέτοιο φάρμακο. Αυτό δε σημαίνει ότι όλοι οι ασθενείς εμφάνισαν παρενέργειες ή ότι η θεραπεία τους απέτυχε. Δείχνει, όμως, πόσο συχνά μπορεί να προκύπτουν περιπτώσεις στις οποίες η γενετική πληροφορία θα μπορούσε να αποδειχθεί χρήσιμη για την επιλογή ή την προσαρμογή της αγωγής. Ποια γνωστά φάρμακα επηρεάζονται από τα γονίδιά μας Ανάμεσα στα φάρμακα που εμφανίστηκαν συχνότερα στην ανάλυση περιλαμβάνονται σκευάσματα που χρησιμοποιούνται ευρέως στην καθημερινή ιατρική πρακτική. Ειδικότερα, οι ερευνητές αναφέρουν: Ονδανσετρόνη: Χρησιμοποιείται για την πρόληψη και την αντιμετώπιση της ναυτίας και του εμέτου. Ιβουπροφαίνη: Γνωστό αντιφλεγμονώδες και αναλγητικό φάρμακο. Ομεπραζόλη και παντοπραζόλη: Χρησιμοποιούνται, μεταξύ άλλων, για την αντιμετώπιση της γαστροοισοφαγικής παλινδρόμησης και της καούρας. Ατορβαστατίνη: Χορηγείται για τη μείωση της χοληστερόλης. Η γενετική πληροφορία μπορεί να βοηθήσει τον γιατρό να αξιολογήσει καλύτερα την αναμενόμενη ανταπόκριση ή την πιθανότητα εμφάνισης παρενεργειών. Σύμφωνα με τον Philip E. Empey, αναπληρωτή καθηγητή στη Φαρμακευτική Σχολή του Πανεπιστημίου Πίτσμπουργκ και επικεφαλής συγγραφέα της μελέτης, περισσότεροι από 300 φαρμακευτικά προϊόντα περιλαμβάνουν ήδη στις οδηγίες τους στοιχεία σχετικά με γενετικές παραλλαγές που ενδέχεται να επηρεάζουν τη χρήση τους. Φαρμακογονιδιωματική: Όταν το DNA καθοδηγεί τη θεραπεία «Πολλοί άνθρωποι έχουν βιώσει την εμπειρία να λαμβάνουν ένα φάρμακο που δε λειτουργεί καλά γι’ αυτούς ή τους προκαλεί κάποια παρενέργεια», επισημαίνει ο δρ. Empey. Όπως εξηγεί, παρ’ ότι πολλοί παράγοντες επηρεάζουν την ανταπόκριση στη φαρμακευτική αγωγή, τα νέα ευρήματα δείχνουν ότι η γενετική μπορεί να παίζει ρόλο σε μεγάλο ποσοστό ασθενών. Αυτή είναι και η βασική φιλοσοφία της ιατρικής ακριβείας: Αντί να βασίζεται αποκλειστικά σε μια ενιαία θεραπευτική προσέγγιση, επιδιώκει να αξιοποιεί τα ιδιαίτερα χαρακτηριστικά κάθε ανθρώπου, ώστε να βελτιώνει τις θεραπευτικές αποφάσεις. Θα μπορούσε μια γενετική εξέταση να αποτρέψει παρενέργειες; Τα ευρήματα αναδεικνύουν τη δυνατότητα αξιοποίησης γενετικών εξετάσεων πριν από τη χορήγηση συγκεκριμένων φαρμάκων. Μία από τις προσεγγίσεις που εξετάζονται είναι ο έλεγχος πολλών γνωστών μεταλλάξεων με μία εξέταση, ώστε τα αποτελέσματα να παραμένουν διαθέσιμα στον ηλεκτρονικό ιατρικό φάκελο του ασθενούς. Έτσι, όταν ο γιατρός χρειάζεται να συνταγογραφήσει κάποιο φάρμακο, θα μπορεί να γνωρίζει εάν υπάρχει γενετικός παράγοντας που ενδέχεται να επηρεάζει την αποτελεσματικότητα ή την ασφάλειά του. Η πληροφορία αυτή θα μπορούσε να οδηγήσει στην επιλογή διαφορετικού φαρμάκου ή την προσαρμογή της δοσολογίας. Η προσέγγιση αυτή αξιοποιείται ήδη σε ορισμένες κλινικές περιπτώσεις, όπως σε ασθενείς που λαμβάνουν πολλά φάρμακα ταυτόχρονα. Μια ακόμη δυνατότητα που αναδεικνύει η μελέτη είναι η ενσωμάτωση αυτοματοποιημένων ειδοποιήσεων στους ηλεκτρονικούς φακέλους υγείας. Δηλαδή, όταν ένας γιατρός επιχειρεί να συνταγογραφήσει φάρμακο που μπορεί να επηρεάζεται από γενετική μετάλλαξη του ασθενούς, το σύστημα θα μπορούσε να εμφανίζει σχετική προειδοποίηση. Τι πρέπει να γνωρίζουν οι ασθενείς Οι ερευνητές τονίζουν ότι όσοι έχουν ήδη πραγματοποιήσει φαρμακογονιδιωματικό έλεγχο είναι σημαντικό να ενημερώνουν τους γιατρούς και τους φαρμακοποιούς τους για τα αποτελέσματα. Η ενσωμάτωση αυτών των πληροφοριών στον ηλεκτρονικό ιατρικό φάκελο μπορεί να αποδειχθεί χρήσιμη όχι μόνο για την τρέχουσα θεραπεία, αλλά και για μελλοντικές συνταγογραφήσεις. Αυτό, βέβαια, δε σημαίνει ότι κάθε ασθενής χρειάζεται γενετική εξέταση πριν λάβει οποιοδήποτε φάρμακο. Η χρησιμότητα του ελέγχου εξαρτάται από το φάρμακο, τα διαθέσιμα επιστημονικά δεδομένα και την κλινική κατάσταση του ασθενούς. «Όπως συμβαίνει με κάθε νέα τεχνολογία, το ζητούμενο είναι η υπεύθυνη εφαρμογή της», σημειώνει ο δρ. Empey. Το βασικό συμπέρασμα της μελέτης είναι ότι τα γονίδιά μας μπορεί να αποτελούν ένα ακόμη πολύτιμο εργαλείο για ασφαλέστερες και αποτελεσματικότερες θεραπείες. Διαβάστε επίσης Πώς μπορούμε να «προλάβουμε» τον καρκίνο μαστού – Τι ρόλο παίζουν γονίδια, στρες και τρόπος ζωής Διαβήτης τύπου 2: Διατροφή και άσκηση «νικούν» ακόμη και τα γονίδια; Τι δείχνει νέα μελέτη Γιατί δεν γερνάμε όλοι με τον ίδιο τρόπο και τον ίδιο ρυθμό – Νέα μελέτη αποκαλύπτει

items.descriptionOriginal: A car brakes suddenly as a two-wheeler slips into the gap ahead. An auto-rickshaw swerves to avoid a bus, while another vehicle edges into the next lane. On Indian roads, where cars, buses, three-wheelers and two-wheelers often share limited space, traffic can change its rhythm in seconds. For urban planners and traffic engineers, understanding this movement is no easy task. Many conventional traffic models assume that vehicles follow lanes and maintain relatively predictable speeds. But Indian roads rarely offer such orderly conditions. Researchers at the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Guwahati are working to bridge this gap. By combining drone footage, automated vehicle tracking and machine learning, they have developed mathematical models that better account for the unpredictable ways vehicles move on Indian roads. Tracking nearly nine million vehicle positions Led by Professor Akhilesh Kumar Maurya from the Department of Civil Engineering, the research team studied traffic on an eight-lane divided highway on the outskirts of Delhi. Using drones equipped with high-resolution cameras, they recorded around five hours of daytime traffic footage in 4K resolution. The videos were then processed using DataFromSky, an automated software that extracts vehicle movements from aerial footage. Led by Professor Akhilesh Kumar Maurya, the IIT Guwahati research could help improve traffic simulations, highway planning and congestion management in India. Photograph: (IIT Guwahati) The result was a dataset of 36,818 vehicles and 8,938,920 vehicle-position data points, captured at 10 frames per second. Researchers categorised the vehicles into six groups: two-wheelers, three-wheelers, cars, buses, heavy commercial vehicles and light commercial vehicles. This gave them a detailed picture of how different vehicles moved, how closely they followed one another and how their speeds changed as traffic became denser. Explaining why India-specific data is necessary, Prof Maurya says, "Traffic conditions in India are different from those in many countries where existing traffic models have been developed. We need traffic data that represents the diversity and characteristics of Indian roads." Drone-based data collection provides an opportunity to observe a large number of vehicles and their movements over a road section at high spatial and temporal resolution. Teaching traffic models to account for unpredictability One interesting finding was that the distance vehicles maintained from one another changed with traffic density. On relatively empty roads, vehicles kept larger gaps. As traffic increased, these gaps became smaller. However, when congestion became severe, the spacing patterns changed again. This variability is important because two vehicles travelling under seemingly similar traffic conditions may not necessarily move at the same speed. Using automated vehicle tracking and machine learning, the researchers mapped 36,818 vehicles and nearly nine million vehicle-position data points. Photograph: ( iStock ) To understand these differences, the researchers tested six mathematical traffic models, including established approaches such as Greenshields and Underwood. They also trained two machine learning models: Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) and Random Forest (RF). But perhaps the most interesting part was their development of stochastic fundamental diagrams. In simple terms, conventional traffic models generally estimate one speed for a given traffic density. Stochastic models go a step further by accounting for the range of speeds that vehicles may actually travel at under those conditions. This allows the models to represent the randomness of Indian traffic more realistically, rather than smoothing over the differences between individual vehicles. From better predictions to smarter road planning The researchers found that the Underwood model performed most consistently among the mathematical models tested, achieving an R² value of 0.86. The two machine learning models achieved approximately 0.83. The research could have practical applications in assessing highway capacity, designing intersections, estimating road speeds, and improving traffic simulations. The data could also help researchers calibrate car-following models, which study how drivers adjust their distance and speed in relation to vehicles ahead. Prof. Maurya explains, "Reliable traffic management begins with models that represent how traffic actually behaves on Indian roads. The high-resolution trajectory data generated through drones allows us to capture interactions among different vehicle types and the large variability that conventional traffic models often overlook." Such India-specific models can support more realistic traffic simulation, better road and intersection design, congestion management, capacity assessment, and the development of intelligent traffic-management systems suited to Indian conditions. Unlike conventional traffic models, the stochastic models developed by the team account for variations in vehicle speeds and distances, even under similar traffic conditions. Photograph: ( Adobe Stock ) For anyone who has spent time on an Indian road, the challenge of predicting traffic is easy to understand. A car slows down, a two-wheeler slips into a narrow gap, an auto-rickshaw changes lanes, and the movement of hundreds of vehicles can shift in seconds. By capturing these interactions in detail, the IIT Guwahati team hopes to make traffic models better reflect what commuters experience every day. The research is a step towards understanding not just how many vehicles use a road, but how they move around one another. And that understanding could eventually help make the daily journey a little more predictable, whether someone is driving to work, taking a bus to school or navigating a crowded intersection.

items.descriptionOriginal: China has set a new Guinness World Record after 151 humanoid robots performed a synchronized dance routine in Shenzhen. The record-setting performance took place on November 17, ahead of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders’ Meeting scheduled for November 18–19 in the southern Chinese technology hub. The robots completed the challenge for the most humanoid robots dancing simultaneously within one hour. The event exceeded its initial target of 110 robots, with Guinness World Records adjudicator Xiong Wen announcing that all 151 machines had completed the performance. Humanoids synchronize moves The Shenzhen Longgang District Artificial Intelligence (Robotics) Bureau led the event and organized it with a robot 6S store, ENGINEAI Robotics Technology, and other robotics companies. ENGINEAI’s full-size T800 humanoid robots played a key role in the demonstration, with 20 units showcasing the company’s swarm-control capabilities. Groups of Unitree G1 and AGIBOT X2 humanoids also participated in the performance. The T800 is a full-size humanoid robot measuring 1.73 meters (5.7 feet) tall and weighing approximately 75 kilograms (165 pounds). According to ENGINEAI, the machine features a high-torque output of 450 newton-meters, allowing it to perform demanding movements that require considerable balance and joint strength. These include spinning kicks, rising dragon punches, kip-ups, and backflip landings, reports Gasgoo. The robot’s ability to perform dynamic movements makes it suitable for demonstrations involving coordinated motion and physical agility. However, the Shenzhen performance also highlighted another important aspect of humanoid robotics: coordinating large numbers of machines to perform the same movements at the same time. Synchronizing multiple humanoid robots requires coordination across their motion-control systems, joint movements, and timing. Maintaining consistent movements across a large group also presents challenges involving stability and the execution of programmed routines. Humanoids welcome APEC The record attempt formed part of a broader effort to showcase Shenzhen’s robotics industry ahead of the APEC summit. During the summit period, ENGINEAI’s T800 and PM01 humanoid robots also participated in several events, demonstrating applications involving entertainment performances, reception services, and smart traffic management. Other robotics companies also brought their machines to public demonstrations across the city. Reports from Shenzhen showed humanoid robots performing synchronized dances, martial arts routines, and other interactive demonstrations for residents and visitors. The city has become an important center for China’s technology industry, hosting major companies such as Huawei, Tencent, BYD, and DJI. Its robotics ecosystem includes developers of industrial automation systems, service robots, and humanoid machines. The APEC gathering brings together 21 member economies representing approximately 60 percent of global economic output. Hosting the meeting allows China to present Shenzhen as a center for technological development and advanced manufacturing. The 151- robot performance was therefore more than an entertainment spectacle. It demonstrated how advances in robotics, motion control, and multi-machine coordination are increasingly being brought into public-facing applications. As humanoid robot developers work toward commercial deployment, demonstrations involving multiple machines could help showcase the potential of coordinated robotic systems in entertainment, manufacturing, and service environments.

items.descriptionOriginal: Happy Eco News Trust and Climate-Smart Agriculture Scaling Depend More on Neighbors Than Institutions, Study Finds Reading Time: 3 minutes A study of 514 Central American farmers found that trust and climate-smart agriculture scaling are closely linked, with relationships with neighbors mattering more than trust in outside organizations. Trust and climate-smart agriculture scaling have long been treated as separate concerns, one social, one technical. New research published in Agricultural Systems directly challenges that separation, showing that farmer-to-farmer relationships shape whether climate innovations spread at all, regardless of how well-designed they are on paper. Researchers from the Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT, the University of Copenhagen, and the Gates Foundation analyzed data from 514 smallholder farmers participating in Climate-Smart Villages, known locally as Territorios Sostenibles Adaptados al Clima, across Guatemala and Honduras. The study examined how different dimensions of social capital influence knowledge sharing about climate-smart practices, and what that process reveals about the earliest stages of responsible scaling. The findings reframe how funders and policymakers should evaluate trust and the scaling of climate-smart agriculture. Success is traditionally measured only after an innovation has already reached large numbers of adopters. This study instead focuses on an earlier moment: when farmers first share experiences, discuss new practices, raise questions, and learn from one another, long before adoption becomes visible at any meaningful scale. Trust among farmers emerged as the single most consistent factor enabling knowledge sharing. When farmers trust one another, they are much more likely to share experiences, discuss new practices, and learn from each other’s successes and failures. Close relationships among farmers further strengthen these learning networks, making it easier for knowledge and hands-on experience to circulate freely within a community rather than remaining isolated within individual households. Perhaps the study’s most striking finding for trust and scaling climate-smart agriculture is the role of mutual support. Researchers found that support between farmers becomes especially critical in communities where trust remains low. In these lower-trust environments, guidance, collaboration, and the exchange of practical experience help sustain knowledge flows that trust alone would otherwise fail to carry. Mutual support effectively functions as a backup mechanism, compensating for weaker social bonds that might otherwise block information sharing entirely. Trust and climate-smart agriculture scaling depend heavily on mutual support in low-trust communities, where researchers found that guidance and collaboration between farmers help sustain the flow of knowledge that institutional trust alone fails to provide. Photo by Frank Meriño on Pexels. By contrast, the research found that trust in formal organizations, whether government agencies, NGOs, or research institutions, carried notably less influence than trust built directly among farmers themselves. This distinction matters enormously for how development programs are typically designed, since many climate-smart agriculture initiatives invest heavily in institutional credibility and extension services while underinvesting in the peer networks that this study identifies as more decisive. Researchers also found a positive association between adopting climate-smart practices and knowledge sharing, reinforcing that these two processes reinforce each other rather than operating independently. A farmer observing a neighbor successfully implementing a drought-coping technique, discussing the results, adapting that practice to their own land’s specific conditions, and later sharing their experience with others exemplifies the kind of organic circulation of trust and climate-smart agriculture scaling research seeks to capture and understand. These findings carry direct implications for how governments, development organizations, and innovation programs design their interventions. The evidence suggests development organizations need to place social dynamics at the center of scaling strategies rather than treating community relationships as secondary to technical training and resource distribution. Programs that invest in building trust and facilitating informal peer networks, rather than relying solely on top-down institutional messaging, appear better positioned to achieve the kind of local ownership that sustains results over time. Trust and climate-smart agriculture scaling research also supports what the study authors describe as a responsible scaling approach, one that anticipates and manages unintended consequences before they emerge rather than addressing problems only after widespread adoption has already occurred. Understanding how knowledge circulates among farmers before adoption becomes visible allows program designers to build strategies that are more inclusive, more context-sensitive, and more attuned to the specific social fabric of the communities they aim to serve. As agrifood systems worldwide face mounting pressure to accelerate climate adaptation, this research corrects purely technical approaches to scaling innovation. The impact of any climate-smart agricultural practice depends not only on its scientific merit, but equally on farmers’ capacity to share knowledge, learn collaboratively, and build the relationships of trust that let that knowledge travel organically through a community, often well before any formal program measures success. The post Trust and Climate-Smart Agriculture Scaling Depend More on Neighbors Than Institutions, Study Finds appeared first on Happy Eco News .

items.descriptionOriginal: This story was originally published by Grist . Sign up for Grist’s weekly newsletter here . Doing the laundry has grown easier and more efficient over the years, yet two things have always remained the same: A washing machine needs water, and a dryer needs heat. Technology designed to clean aerospace parts reimagines the process by ditching both of those in favor of an unlikely substitute: carbon dioxide, the very gas we’re trying so hard to contain. Under pressure, CO2 becomes a low-viscosity liquid capable of penetrating fabrics and carrying away oils and grime. When depressurized, it reverts to a gas, leaving clothes clean and dry. No wastewater. No dryer. Beyond its novelty, the idea could clean up a resource-intensive chore. The average family runs roughly 300 loads a year, consuming thousands of gallons of water. And more than 80 percent of U.S. households own a dryer, with one study putting the annual CO2 emissions from machine drying alone at 27 million metric tons . Tersus Solutions’ industrial CO2 washers use high pressure to turn carbon dioxide into a liquid that can clean fabrics without water. The machines’ bulky pressure chambers, pumps, pipes and compressors illustrate the challenge appliance makers face in trying to shrink the technology for household use. Courtesy of Teresus Solutions Long confined to industrial operations, liquid-CO2 cleaning is getting a second look from appliance giants LG and Samsung — this time for the home. Still, shrinking a technology built around bulky, high-pressure machinery to fit both a laundry room and household budget is a tall order. No less challenging is doing so without washing away the environmental gains that make waterless, dryerless laundry so enticing in the first place. Just getting this far has taken decades. Hughes Aircraft developed the process in 1990 to remove grease and other contaminants from electronic components. Electrolux later pursued it as a safer alternative to solvent-based dry cleaning, though cost, complexity, and bulky equipment kept it from catching on. In 2009, Colorado-based Tersus Solutions began refining the technology and has since carved out a niche cleaning outdoor apparel and equipment, as well as firefighter gear contaminated with hazardous residues. Its machines offer a glimpse of what CO2 cleaning can do and why squeezing it into a household appliance is no simple feat. Weighed down by negative news? Enter your email below to receive our smart, uplifting newsletters. Or click here to choose exactly which ones you want [contact-form-7] Tersus CEO Peter Whitcomb describes the machines as “futuristic front-loading washers,” though the company’s two models dwarf those found in a typical laundromat. Each occupies a roughly 10-foot cube, with the larger unit handling up to 85 pounds of laundry, or a dozen sleeping bags. Behind a thick, submarine-like hatch, a rotating drum sits inside a pressurized chamber amid a maze of pipes, pumps and compressors. Despite the complexity, what happens inside is relatively simple. Carbon dioxide turns from gas to liquid at 900 pounds per square inch of pressure — roughly one-third of what’s inside a full scuba tank . As it circulates, filters trap the grime, which accumulates as a thick purplish sludge for disposal. When the 45-minute cycle ends, the pressure drops and liquid returns to gas, instantly drying the load. More than 90 percent of the CO2 is recaptured for the next run; the rest escapes in a smoky wisp. The process is particularly effective on firefighter gear, with tests showing an average of more than 95 percent removal of contaminants such as PAHs, potentially harmful compounds found in smoke and soot. Water-soluble stains from sweat and food can be trickier, said Chris Robbins, Tersus’ chief technology officer, occasionally requiring pretreatment — “think Tide pen, but for CO2” — or conventional washing. For most loads, however, the process eliminates water and additives alike. “We’re not using detergent, we don’t use heat,” Whitcomb said. Tersus estimates its larger machines save roughly 300 gallons of water per load compared with conventional washing. There is another potential upside, as well: By eliminating wastewater and trapping shed fibers for disposal, the process could further reduce microplastic contamination from laundry. The energy equation, however, is more complicated. A California Energy Commission demonstration with the U.S. Navy found the method used about 15 percent less energy than smaller commercial washers and dryers, yet about as much as larger industrial combinations. Tersus has found comparable performance, said Robbins. While CO2 cleaning avoids thermal drying — typically the most energy-intensive part of conventional laundry — removing impurities from the carbon dioxide for reuse requires significant power. The company is exploring more efficient ways of heating and cooling the gas, Robbins said. As for the CO2, Tersus gets it from a nearby ethanol plant, where it’s a byproduct of fermentation. That minimizes transportation needs, although purifying and liquefying it require additional energy — further complicating the calculation of the technology’s overall carbon footprint. Then there’s the question of scale: Could all that machinery — enough to fill a small bedroom — be shrunk into a household appliance? LG and Samsung are working on that. Recent patents from the companies, both of which declined to comment, tackle distinct challenges: removing stains resistant to CO2 cleaning and reducing the pressure required to make the tech work. LG’s design uses detergents and other additives to help remove water-soluble stains. Although the patent doesn’t specify a formula, a recent study found that adding isopropyl alcohol and water improved liquid carbon dioxide’s ability to remove sugars, salts and other compounds. Samsung, meanwhile, proposes combining CO2 with other solvents to bring operating pressures down to a fraction of those used in industrial machines. That could make home models more compact, though some of the mixtures include PFAS , raising questions about environmental trade-offs. Smaller, however, doesn’t necessarily mean simpler. Separating and recovering those added solvents could require still more equipment, said Eckhard Groll, head of mechanical engineering at Purdue University and an expert in CO2 refrigeration. “There’s no question” that a home version is technically feasible, he said, “but it may be very costly, the technology.” Even if the machines become affordable, the environmental benefits may not carry over, said Rainer Stamminger, a household appliance efficiency researcher at the University of Bonn. With households running just a few loads a week, pressurizing and recovering carbon dioxide could be “very inefficient just for one wash” compared to industrial machines that run continuously. The economics may be especially challenging in the U.S., where electricity is relatively cheap. Groll pointed to heat pump dryers, which use about half the energy of conventional electric models. Popular in Europe, they made up 75 percent of new dryer sales in 2020, helped by higher electricity prices that helped ease the sticker shock; meanwhile, American sales still lag . CO2 washers could as well if their efficiency comes with a hefty upfront premium. Whitcomb sees greater opportunities in commercial dry cleaning, apartment buildings and institutions, where higher volumes could justify the equipment costs — and keep the machines running often enough to take advantage of their scale. With a new facility in Calgary expanding its Colorado operations, Tersus now works with more than 40 brands and retailers, offering repairs, restoration and resale services that “complement the cleaning” to extend garment life and keep products in circulation, Whitcomb said. Wait, you're not a member yet? Join the Reasons to be Cheerful community by supporting our nonprofit publication and giving what you can. Join Cancel anytime Even if engineers can make a home CO2 washer affordable and efficient, they would still have to convince people to buy one. The early market for water-efficient front-load washers offers a precedent: Energy and water savings attracted some consumers, while upfront costs deterred others. Performance and convenience mattered, too, said Gwendolyn Hustvedt, a textiles and consumer sciences professor at Texas State University who studied the trend. The technology may have one big selling point, however: The clothes come out dry. Beyond saving time and hassle, skipping what Hustvedt called “cooking your clothes in a box” could help garments last longer by reducing shrinkage and wear from heat and tumbling. Whether consumers would pay a premium for those benefits is another question. Home CO2 washers still have a long way to go before they break up the familiar washer-dryer combo. But if engineers can make the physics work economically — and environmentally — at household scale, the next big thing in laundry might be one less appliance. items.descriptionOriginal: Οι άνδρες εξακολουθούν να έχουν μικρότερο προσδόκιμο ζωής από τις γυναίκες , ενώ εμφανίζουν υψηλότερη θνησιμότητα από συγκεκριμένες μορφές καρκίνου, καρδιαγγειακά νοσήματα και ατυχήματα. Με αφορμή την Παγκόσμια Ημέρα Ανδρών , στις 19 Νοεμβρίου, πρόσφατα στοιχεία από την Ομοσπονδιακή Στατιστική Υπηρεσία της Γερμανίας (Destatis), τα οποία παρουσιάστηκαν στο Medscape τον Νοέμβριο του 2026, αναδεικνύουν σημαντικές διαφορές μεταξύ των δύο φύλων και υπογραμμίζουν την ανάγκη ενίσχυσης της πρόληψης. Οι Ιατροί της Θεραπευτικής Κλινικής (Νοσοκομείο Αλεξάνδρα) της Ιατρικής Σχολής του ΕΚΠΑ Θεοδώρα Ψαλτοπούλου (Καθηγήτρια Θεραπευτικής – Επιδημιολογίας – Προληπτικής Ιατρικής, Παθολόγος), Δρ. Μαρία Καπαρέλου (Παθολόγος – Ογκολόγος) και Θάνος Δημόπουλος (Καθηγητής Θεραπευτικής – Ογκολογίας – Αιματολογίας, Διευθυντής Θεραπευτικής Κλινικής, Νοσοκομείο «Αλεξάνδρα», τ. Πρύτανης ΕΚΠΑ) αναφέρουν ότι σύμφωνα με τα διαθέσιμα δεδομένα, η θνησιμότητα των ανδρών είναι υψηλότερη σε όλες τις ηλικιακές ομάδες. Η διαφορά είναι ιδιαίτερα έντονη στις ηλικίες 15–34 ετών, όπου οι θάνατοι των ανδρών είναι υπερδιπλάσιοι εκείνων των γυναικών. Στις ηλικίες 35–84 ετών, η θνησιμότητα των ανδρών είναι κατά 50%–85% υψηλότερη. Το προσδόκιμο ζωής στη Γερμανία διαμορφώνεται στα 78,8 έτη για τους άνδρες και στα 83,4 έτη για τις γυναίκες, παρουσιάζοντας διαφορά 4,6 ετών. Παρά τη σταδιακή μείωση αυτής της απόκλισης τις τελευταίες δεκαετίες, οι ανισότητες παραμένουν σημαντικές. Τα καρδιαγγειακά νοσήματα αποτελούν μία από τις κυριότερες αιτίες αυξημένης ανδρικής θνησιμότητας. Σύμφωνα με τα στοιχεία της Destatis, καταγράφηκαν 65.435 θάνατοι ανδρών από ισχαιμική καρδιοπάθεια, έναντι 48.038 γυναικών. Αντίστοιχα, οι θάνατοι από έμφραγμα του μυοκαρδίου ανήλθαν σε 24.875 και 16.383. Παρότι η θνησιμότητα από έμφραγμα παρουσιάζει πτωτική τάση, παράγοντες όπως το κάπνισμα, η αρτηριακή υπέρταση, η δυσλιπιδαιμία, ο σακχαρώδης διαβήτης, η παχυσαρκία και η σωματική αδράνεια εξακολουθούν να επιβαρύνουν σημαντικά την καρδιαγγειακή υγεία. Σημαντικές διαφορές παρατηρούνται και στη θνησιμότητα από καρκίνο . Το 2025, ο καρκίνος του πνεύμονα ευθυνόταν για 26.192 θανάτους ανδρών, έναντι 18.972 γυναικών, αποτελώντας τη δεύτερη συχνότερη αιτία θανάτου στους άνδρες. Η διαχρονικά υψηλότερη κατανάλωση καπνού στον ανδρικό πληθυσμό αποτελεί καθοριστικό παράγοντα αυτής της διαφοράς. Παράλληλα, ο καρκίνος του παχέος εντέρου προκάλεσε 12.554 θανάτους ανδρών και 10.336 γυναικών. Εκτός από την ηλικία και τη γενετική προδιάθεση, η παχυσαρκία, η έλλειψη σωματικής δραστηριότητας, η κατανάλωση αλκοόλ και ορισμένες διατροφικές συνήθειες συμβάλλουν στην εμφάνιση της νόσου. Τα δεδομένα αυτά αναδεικνύουν τη σημασία της διακοπής του καπνίσματος, της υιοθέτησης υγιεινών συνηθειών και της συμμετοχής σε προγράμματα προσυμπτωματικού ελέγχου . Ιδιαίτερη σημασία έχει η εξατομικευμένη αξιολόγηση του κινδύνου για καρκίνο του παχέος εντέρου, του πνεύμονα και του προστάτη, σύμφωνα με τις ενδεδειγμένες συστάσεις πρόληψης. Ένας ακόμη σημαντικός παράγοντας κινδύνου είναι η κατανάλωση αλκοόλ. Το 2023 καταγράφηκαν περίπου 169.800 νοσηλείες ανδρών για ψυχικές και συμπεριφορικές διαταραχές σχετιζόμενες με το αλκοόλ, έναντι 62.900 στις γυναίκες. Τα στοιχεία αφορούν περιστατικά νοσηλείας και όχι μοναδικούς ασθενείς. Η κατανάλωση αλκοόλ συνδέεται με αυξημένο κίνδυνο κακοηθειών, καρδιαγγειακών νοσημάτων, ηπατικής βλάβης και ατυχημάτων. Ιδιαίτερα ανησυχητική είναι η υπερεκπροσώπηση των ανδρών στα θανατηφόρα ατυχήματα. Το 2025, το 73,6% των θυμάτων τροχαίων δυστυχημάτων στη Γερμανία ήταν άνδρες. Στις ηλικίες 15–20 ετών, οι θάνατοι αγοριών και νεαρών ανδρών ήταν περίπου πενταπλάσιοι εκείνων των κοριτσιών και νεαρών γυναικών. Η υπερβολική ταχύτητα, η οδήγηση υπό την επήρεια αλκοόλ ή άλλων ουσιών και η συχνότερη χρήση μοτοσικλετών συμβάλλουν σε αυτή τη διαφορά. Ανάλογη εικόνα καταγράφεται στους πνιγμούς . Σύμφωνα με τα στοιχεία της Γερμανικής Ένωσης Ναυαγοσωστικής (DLRG), έως τον Σεπτέμβριο του 2026 σχεδόν το 85% των θυμάτων ήταν άνδρες. Η υποτίμηση του κινδύνου, η υπερεκτίμηση των προσωπικών δυνατοτήτων, οι ανεπαρκείς κολυμβητικές δεξιότητες και η κατανάλωση αλκοόλ αποτελούν σημαντικούς επιβαρυντικούς παράγοντες. Η μικρότερη διάρκεια ζωής των ανδρών δεν μπορεί να αποδοθεί αποκλειστικά σε βιολογικές διαφορές. Οι συμπεριφορικές συνήθειες, οι κοινωνικές επιδράσεις, οι επαγγελματικές επιβαρύνσεις και η περιορισμένη αξιοποίηση των υπηρεσιών υγείας διαδραματίζουν επίσης ουσιαστικό ρόλο. Το κεντρικό μήνυμα της Παγκόσμιας Ημέρας Ανδρών είναι ότι σ ημαντικό μέρος της πρόωρης ανδρικής θνησιμότητας μπορεί να προληφθεί. Η έγκαιρη αναγνώριση και αντιμετώπιση των παραγόντων κινδύνου, ο συστηματικός προληπτικός έλεγχος, η φροντίδα της ψυχικής υγείας και η υιοθέτηση ασφαλέστερων συμπεριφορών μπορούν να συμβάλουν ουσιαστικά στη βελτίωση τόσο της διάρκειας όσο και της ποιότητας ζωής. Η πρόληψη πρέπει να ξεκινά από τη νεαρή ηλικία, πολύ πριν εμφανιστούν σοβαρά προβλήματα υγείας. Διαβάστε επίσης Οι 8 στους 10 άνδρες αποφεύγουν να μιλήσουν για την ψυχική τους υγεία – Γιατί συμβαίνει αυτό Γιατί οι άνδρες διαγιγνώσκονται συχνότερα με καρκίνο σε προχωρημένο στάδιο Ποιος είναι ο συχνότερος καρκίνος σε άνδρες 15-40 ετών – Οι παράγοντες κινδύνου

items.descriptionOriginal: Happy Eco News Watershed Restoration in Ethiopia Reaches First Major Milestone Reading Time: 3 minutes Watershed restoration in Ethiopia reached a new milestone as 1,000 community members planted 152,333 seedlings across four degraded micro-watersheds in the Tana Subbasin. Watershed restoration in Ethiopia reached a new milestone in July, with more than 1,000 community members planting over 150,000 tree seedlings across four degraded micro-watersheds . The effort marks ProTana’s first major field campaign, a five-year project led by the World Resources Institute and partners. Nearly half of the volunteers were women. ProTana focuses on the Tana Subbasin in Ethiopia’s Amhara Region, home to Lake Tana, the country’s largest lake and the source of the Blue Nile. The lake and its surrounding watersheds supply water for millions of people across the region. Decades of deforestation, overgrazing, and soil erosion have steadily degraded the land feeding into it. Lake Tana’s importance reaches well beyond Ethiopia’s borders. Water flowing out of the lake eventually joins the Blue Nile, which supplies a significant share of the water reaching Sudan and Egypt downstream. Keeping the watersheds that feed the lake healthy therefore affects water security across the wider Nile basin, not just the communities living closest to it. The World Resources Institute (WRI) is implementing the project alongside WaterAid Ethiopia and ORDA Ethiopia, focusing on three districts: North Mecha, Farta, and Dera. Selecting which specific watersheds to restore took months of consultation with local officials and community leaders. Criteria included erosion severity, the importance of water supply, and each community’s willingness to participate. The four selected micro-watersheds span more than 2,100 hectares combined. During July’s planting campaign, workers and volunteers put in over 152,000 seedlings, split between private agroforestry plots and communal or institutional land. Planting took place at the start of Ethiopia’s main rainy season to give seedlings the best chance of survival. Community turnout exceeded expectations, with more than 1,000 people taking part directly. Many children and young people also attended, watched the planting process, and learned why restoring the land matters for their future water security. Organizers see early engagement as key to building long-term support, since restoration work without community buy-in rarely survives past its first planting season. Watershed restoration in Ethiopia drew more than 1,000 community participants, with children and young people watching and learning alongside adults, as organizers bet that early engagement is the only way to build the long-term community buy-in that keeps restoration work alive past its first planting season. Photo by Khedir Dawed, courtesy of World Resources Institute . This campaign builds on an earlier three-year pilot in the Minzir 01 micro-watershed, part of the same broader area. That pilot showed measurable improvements in local water supply alongside benefits for nearby crop farming. ProTana now aims to apply those same lessons across a much larger area. Tree planting represents only the first phase of watershed restoration in Ethiopia under this project. Future work will include soil and water conservation measures such as terracing, check dams, and soil bunds. Regenerative agricultural practices are also planned to help households manage land more sustainably over the long term. A WRI program specialist working on the project described success as depending heavily on strong local leadership and coordination between partners. He noted that when communities see real benefits firsthand, they tend to stay far more committed to protecting restored land afterward, rather than treating conservation as an outside obligation imposed on them. According to the World Resources Institute, watershed restoration in Ethiopia fits into a broader strategy addressing water risk, climate resilience, and sustainable water governance across the country. The organization continues to monitor seedling survival through the rainy season to track how well the new plantings take hold. If ProTana’s larger rollout matches the results seen in its earlier pilot, this round of watershed restoration in Ethiopia could improve water availability and livelihoods for thousands of households in the Tana Subbasin. Much of that outcome will depend on how well new seedlings survive and how consistently local institutions keep up conservation work after the initial planting rush ends. For now, the scale of community turnout offers an early, encouraging sign that residents are ready to stay involved for the long haul. items.descriptionOriginal: Once known as the Garden City for its tree-lined avenues, blooming parks and pleasant weather, Bengaluru is now facing a growing question: How can a rapidly expanding city make room for nature while preparing for heavier rains, water shortages and rising temperatures? Now, a neighbourhood-level climate planning exercise across five wards aims to address some of these concerns through better drainage, rainwater management and urban greening. The Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) has prepared ward-level Climate Action Plans for five pilot wards across the city, identifying environmental challenges and proposing interventions suited to the conditions of each neighbourhood. The initiative is now awaiting budgetary approval from the respective city corporations before implementation can begin. The five wards selected for the pilot are Shantinagar in Central Bengaluru, Jakkur in the North, Begur in the South, Vijinapura in the East and Nalwadi Krishnaraja Wadiyar ward in the West. Developed under the GBA's Climate Action Cell, the plans aim to take climate planning beyond city-wide recommendations and identify what individual neighbourhoods need. The assessments cover energy and buildings, transportation, solid waste management, urban planning, greenery and biodiversity, water management, wastewater and stormwater management, and disaster preparedness. According to The New Indian Express, the plans were prepared following sector-wise assessments and consultations with residents, experts and other stakeholders. The exercise recognises that climate-related challenges are not uniform across Bengaluru. While some localities experience recurring flooding, others face water scarcity, declining green cover, rising temperatures or inadequate waste management. Why Bengaluru needs neighbourhood-level climate planning The city's contrasting water challenges illustrate why localised planning matters. Bengaluru experiences heavy surface runoff during the monsoon, even as several neighbourhoods face groundwater depletion and water shortages during summer. A March 18, 2026 report by Mongabay-India, which examined the ward-level planning exercise, highlighted how geography influences flood vulnerability. For instance, Shantinagar, a densely populated urban ward, lies in a downstream valley zone. Hydrological assessments by WELL Labs and Bengaluru's Climate Action Cell found that floodwater can originate beyond the ward's boundaries, making flooding a problem that cannot always be addressed through isolated drainage work within one locality. The five-ward pilot is intended to provide a model for extending climate action planning to other neighbourhoods under the GBA. Photograph: (Bengaluru Climate Action Cell-via Mongabay) Anam Husain, programme associate for Urban Water at WELL Labs, told Mongabay-India that nature-based interventions such as rain gardens, bioswales, permeable surfaces and small retention systems can help slow down rainwater runoff and improve groundwater infiltration. These interventions offer ways to manage excess rainwater closer to where it falls, while also reducing pressure on conventional drainage infrastructure. Rainwater harvesting and groundwater recharge are particularly relevant in a city where water scarcity and monsoon runoff exist side by side. Alongside improving stormwater management, wastewater reuse and stormwater reuse can contribute to longer-term water security. Bringing green infrastructure into urban planning Urban greening is another important component of Bengaluru's climate planning exercise. In neighbourhoods experiencing rising temperatures, the GBA is considering measures such as increasing green cover, using heat-reflective cool paints and establishing cool shelters. These interventions can help address the urban heat island effect , in which built-up areas with extensive concrete surfaces and limited vegetation retain more heat than surrounding areas. Bengaluru's existing Climate Action and Resilience Plan also identifies nature-based solutions as an important part of urban development. View this post on Instagram A post shared by ಬೆಂಗಳೂರು ದಕ್ಷಿಣ ನಗರ ಪಾಲಿಕೆ (Bengaluru South City Corporation) (@bscc.gba) Its sectoral recommendations include restoring the city's blue-green networks, increasing tree canopy and expanding green and permeable surfaces to help reduce flood and heat-related risks. The plan sets targets to increase the city's tree canopy by 10% from its baseline by 2030 and 20% by 2040. It also proposes increasing green cover and permeable surfaces to 40% of the city's area by 2040. From climate plans to neighbourhood-level action Public participation has also been part of the planning process. Just recently, The Better India documented how Bengaluru residents are taking small, collective steps to care for their city's shared spaces . From removing 110 kg of plastic waste around Madiwala Lake during a 75-minute plogging drive to watering hundreds of saplings at Vengaiah Lake through the Bhagiratha initiative, the report highlighted how citizen participation can complement urban conservation efforts. Read the report. Other efforts include residents in Balagere, Panathur and Varthur clearing accumulated roadside dust, and volunteers working with civic authorities to restore neglected footpaths and public spaces. The Greater Bengaluru Authority's proposed Climate Action Plans across five wards take this approach further by seeking to integrate local environmental needs into formal urban planning. The five-ward pilot is intended to provide a model for extending climate action planning to other neighbourhoods under the GBA. For Bengaluru, the next step will be translating these local assessments into funded projects that improve drainage, strengthen water management and expand green infrastructure. The effectiveness of the exercise will ultimately depend on how consistently these proposals are implemented and monitored at the neighbourhood level. Sources: 'GBA goes micro local with ward-level climate plans' : By Express News Service, Published on 4 November 2026 'Ward-level plans bring climate action closer to communities' : By Mahima Jain, Published on 18 March 2026

items.title: Η Rolls-Royce SMR δοκιμάζει εργοστασιακή υποστήριξη για την προστασία των πυρηνικών σταθμών από σεισμούς
items.titleOriginal: Rolls-Royce SMR tests factory-built support to protect nuclear plants from earthquakes
items.description: Η Rolls-Royce SMR ολοκλήρωσε μια σημαντική δοκιμή κατασκευής για το πρόγραμμα μικρών αρθρωτών αντιδραστήρων (SMR). Ένα νέο προκατασκευασμένο εξάρτημα από σκυρόδεμα θα μπορούσε να βοηθήσει στη διευκόλυνση της κατασκευής και συναρμολόγησης μελλοντικών πυρηνικών σταθμών. Η Skanska κατασκεύασε και δοκίμασε ένα σεισμικό βάθρο ρουλεμάν στις εγκαταστάσεις της Bentley Works στο Doncaster της Αγγλίας. Ο επίδειξης επικυρώνει ένα…
items.descriptionOriginal: Rolls-Royce SMR has completed an important construction test for its small modular reactor (SMR) program. A new precast concrete component could help make future nuclear plants easier to manufacture and assemble. Skanska built and tested an aseismic bearing pedestal at its Bentley Works facility in Doncaster, England. The demonstrator validates an off-site manufacturing approach for a component that plays a crucial role in protecting nuclear infrastructure during earthquakes. The achievement gives Rolls-Royce SMR another construction method to evaluate before deploying its factory-built reactor design. It also demonstrates how conventional construction techniques could support the industrial-scale production of nuclear power plants. Testing earthquake protection Aseismic bearing pedestals support isolation devices within the Rolls-Royce SMR design. These devices help separate buildings and other structures from ground movement during seismic events. The isolation system reduces the forces that earthquakes can transfer into critical infrastructure. Its performance therefore plays an important role in protecting the reactor facility and supporting its structural resilience. Skanska’s demonstrator allowed engineers to test the manufacturing approach before committing to full-scale deployment. Producing the component away from the construction site could also give manufacturers greater control over quality and production schedules. The prototype represents a first-of-its-kind precast bearing pedestal for the Rolls-Royce SMR design. Skanska completed its construction and technical trials at Bentley Works, bringing its engineering and manufacturing capabilities into the project. Factory production takes shape Off-site manufacturing forms an important part of the Rolls-Royce SMR construction strategy. The company wants to move significant portions of plant construction into controlled manufacturing environments. That approach could reduce the amount of work required at individual construction sites. It could also improve consistency across multiple reactors by allowing suppliers to repeat established manufacturing processes. Rolls-Royce SMR Operations and Supply Chain Director Ruth Todd said the demonstrator supports the company’s plans for factory-built nuclear plants. She also pointed to the importance of testing critical components before deployment. Early cooperation with suppliers helps engineers identify potential problems before construction begins. It also gives manufacturers time to refine their processes ahead of larger production requirements. Skanska UK Executive Vice President Terry Muckian highlighted the engineering work behind the demonstrator. The project combined the contractor’s civil engineering, design and steelwork manufacturing experience. UK nuclear plans advance Rolls-Royce SMR has secured a place in the UK’s small modular reactor deployment program through Great British Energy – Nuclear. The country’s first planned deployment will take place at Wylfa on Anglesey, North Wales. The UK expects the site to generate its first electricity in the mid-2030s. The Czech Republic and Sweden also feature in the company’s international deployment plans. Small modular reactors use factory-manufactured sections that engineers assemble at their final locations. This approach aims to make nuclear construction more repeatable than conventional projects. The bearing pedestal demonstrator addresses one part of that challenge. Its successful trials give Rolls-Royce SMR and Skanska a tested manufacturing approach for a component that supports seismic protection. Further engineering and manufacturing work will determine how the method translates into future plant construction. The broader objective remains consistent production across a fleet of reactors.

items.title: Το πρώτο εργοστάσιο στον κόσμο που παράγει γραφίτη για μπαταρία από φυσικό αέριο ξεκινά τη λειτουργία του

items.descriptionOriginal: A US startup has begun operating what it describes as the world’s first plant to produce battery-grade graphite from natural gas, opening a new route to manufacturing a critical material used in electric vehicle batteries. Molten Industries commissioned its demonstration facility in Oakland, California, on November 18. The plant uses methane pyrolysis to convert natural gas into graphite and hydrogen, potentially creating a domestic alternative to conventional graphite production. The facility has an annual production capacity of 300 metric tons of graphite anode material. It uses a single modular reactor, with the company reporting natural gas-to-graphite yields above 95 percent. Graphite is a key component of lithium-ion batteries, forming the anode that stores and releases electrical charge. It is widely used in electric vehicles, grid storage systems, and consumer electronics. The US remains heavily dependent on overseas suppliers for battery-grade graphite. China controls around 75 percent of the global graphite anode supply chain and 97 percent of synthetic graphite anode production, according to Benchmark Mineral Intelligence figures cited by TechCrunch . Splitting methane into materials Molten’s process uses methane, the main component of natural gas, as its feedstock. Instead of burning the gas, the technology heats it without oxygen, separating its carbon and hydrogen components. The carbon is processed into graphite suitable for battery anodes, while the hydrogen can be used in industrial applications such as fertilizer production, petroleum refining, methanol manufacturing, and steelmaking. The company says its process uses four times cheaper feedstock and three times less electricity than conventional synthetic graphite production. It also claims the technology eliminates the need for a graphitization furnace, which is used to convert carbon materials into highly crystalline graphite. Molten uses electrical resistive heating to drive the reaction. The company says the process produces no direct process emissions because methane is split without combustion. However, this does not mean the entire production chain is emissions-free. Emissions associated with natural gas extraction, transportation, and electricity generation would still need to be considered when assessing its overall environmental footprint. Scaling domestic graphite supply The Oakland plant is intended to demonstrate that the technology can operate continuously and provide a modular blueprint for larger facilities. According to TechCrunch, the plant’s annual output could supply enough graphite for around 300 megawatt-hours of batteries, equivalent to approximately 4,300 electric vehicles . Most of its production will go to undisclosed customers testing the material in battery cells. That customer validation will be important in determining whether the graphite can meet manufacturers’ requirements for battery performance and consistency. Molten also plans to make samples of its MG Series battery-anode graphite available from December 1, 2026. The company has not announced details of its next production facility, although it says future plants will build on the Oakland reactor design. The technology builds on more than a century of research into methane decomposition. Splitting natural gas into carbon and hydrogen was patented in the late 19th century, but producing high-quality graphite through the process has remained a challenge. Molten’s demonstration plant marks a step toward commercializing that approach. Whether it can compete with established graphite producers will depend on scaling production, proving material quality, and demonstrating competitive costs.
